facts.statement: Paranthodon lived during the Early Cretaceous, with a possible Late Jurassic record.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Early Cretaceous, Possible Late Jurassic record

facts.statement: Paranthodon was discovered in 1845 and was one of the first stegosaurians ever found.
facts.quote: Discovered in 1845, it was one of the first stegosaurians found.

facts.statement: British paleontologist Richard Owen initially misidentified the fossil fragments as belonging to the pareiasaur Anthodon.
facts.quote: British paleontologist Richard Owen initially identified the fragments as those of the pareiasaur Anthodon.

facts.statement: South African paleontologist Robert Broom named the specimen Palaeoscincus africanus after identifying it as a distinct genus.
facts.quote: he named the specimen Palaeoscincus africanus.

facts.statement: Hungarian paleontologist Franz Nopcsa named the taxon Paranthodon owenii without knowing about Robert Broom's earlier name.
facts.quote: Hungarian paleontologist Franz Nopcsa, unaware of Broom's new name, similarly concluded that it represented a new taxon, and named it Paranthodon owenii.

facts.statement: Franz Nopcsa classified Paranthodon as a stegosaurid in 1929, a classification supported by most modern studies.
facts.quote: In 1929, Nopcsa identified the taxon as a stegosaurid, with which most modern studies agree.

facts.statement: A 2018 review found no diagnostic stegosaurian features in Paranthodon, though it was still referred to Stegosauria based on similarity and phylogenetic analysis.
facts.quote: A 2018 review of Paranthodon could only identify one distinguishing feature, and while that study still referred it to Stegosauria based on similarity and multiple phylogenetic analyses, no diagnostic features of the group could be identified in Paranthodon.

facts.statement: Amateur geologists William Guybon Atherstone and Andrew Geddes Bain discovered Paranthodon fossils near Dassieklip in the Bushman's River Valley in 1845.
facts.quote: In 1845, amateur geologists William Guybon Atherstone and Andrew Geddes Bain discovered several fossils near Dassieklip, Cape Province, in the Bushman's River Valley.

facts.statement: Richard Owen named the specimens Anthodon serrarius in 1876, basing the name on the resemblance of the teeth to a flower.
facts.quote: In 1876 Owen named a series of specimens from the collection Anthodon serrarius, basing the generic name on the resemblance of the teeth to a flower.

facts.statement: Robert Broom concluded in 1909 that Richard Owen had mixed fossils from a pareiasaur and a dinosaur, specifically the partial skull and jaw BMNH 47338.
facts.quote: In 1909, Robert Broom visited the collection of the British Museum of Natural History. He concluded that Owen had mixed the partial distorted skull, teeth, and a mandible of a pareiasaur and a partial upper jaw of a dinosaur, BMNH 47338, which were from two different species.

facts.statement: Robert Broom identified the dinosaur fossil as Palaeoscincus africanus in 1912 while keeping the name Anthodon for the pareiasaur.
facts.quote: Broom kept the name Anthodon for the pareiasaur, but identified the other fossil as a member of the genus Palaeoscincus, naming the new species Palaeoscincus africanus in 1912.

facts.statement: Franz Nopcsa derived the genus name Paranthodon from the Latin word 'para' meaning 'similar' or 'near' and named the species after Richard Owen.
facts.quote: Nopcsa named the species Paranthodon Owenii, with the generic name derived from the Latin para, meaning "similar", "near", or "beside", and Anthodon, and specific name honouring Owen.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen BMNH 47338 was found in the Kirkwood Formation, dated to the Berriasian and early Valanginian ages.
facts.quote: The holotype of Paranthodon, BMNH 47338, was found in a layer of the Kirkwood Formation that has been dated between the Berriasian and early Valanginian ages.

facts.statement: The holotype consists of the back of the snout with the maxilla and teeth, parts of the premaxilla and nasals, and isolated teeth likely from the lower jaw.
facts.quote: It consists of the back of the snout, containing the maxilla with teeth, the posterior caudodorsal ramus of the premaxilla, part of the nasals, and some isolated teeth probably from the lower jaw.

facts.statement: The teeth of Paranthodon lack unique distinguishing features and were referred to an indeterminate stegosaurid in 2008.
facts.quote: The teeth do not bear any autapomorphies of Paranthodon, and were referred to an indeterminate stegosaurid in 2008.

facts.statement: In 2018, the teeth were identified as lacking distinct stegosaurian features and were designated as Thyreophora indeterminate.
facts.quote: The teeth were identified in 2018 as also lacking any distinct stegosaurian features, and were thus designated as Thyreophora indeterminate.

facts.statement: Multiple dinosaur teeth were discovered in the Mugher Mudstone of Ethiopia during screening by the University of California Museum of Paleontology in the 1990s.
facts.quote: The Mugher Mudstone of Ethiopia was screened in the 1990s by the University of California Museum of Paleontology, and in it were discovered multiple dinosaur teeth, pertaining to many groups of taxa.

facts.statement: Lee Hall and Mark Goodwin referred two partial teeth from the Mugher Mudstone to Paranthodon in 2011.
facts.quote: Two of the partial teeth discovered were referred to Paranthodon by Lee Hall and Mark Goodwin in 2011.

facts.statement: A 1981 review using modern taxonomic techniques confirmed Paranthodon as a valid genus of stegosaurid.
facts.quote: In 1981, the genus was reviewed with modern taxonomic techniques, and found to be a valid genus of stegosaurid.

facts.statement: Thomas R. Holtz Jr. estimated Paranthodon was 16.4 feet long and weighed between 454 and 907 kilograms.
facts.quote: Thomas R. Holtz Jr. estimated that the animal was 16.4 ft long and weighed between 454 and 907 kg.

facts.statement: Paranthodon had an elongated snout that was convex on top.
facts.quote: The snout is elongated, though not extremely so, and convex on top.

facts.statement: Paranthodon's teeth featured a prominent primary ridge.
facts.quote: The teeth have a prominent primary ridge.

facts.statement: Thirteen teeth are preserved in Paranthodon, though the animal likely had more in life.
facts.quote: Thirteen teeth are preserved in Paranthodon, but as they extend to the back of the maxilla there were possibly more in life.

facts.statement: Evidence suggests Paranthodon likely lacked occlusion between teeth, as wear is absent on most preserved teeth.
facts.quote: Paranthodon teeth preserve wear, but wear is absent on most teeth, similar to Huayangosaurus, meaning it is likely that Paranthodon lacked occlusion between teeth.

facts.statement: The incomplete premaxilla of Paranthodon has an anterior process that is sinuous and curves ventrally.
facts.quote: The premaxilla of Paranthodon is incomplete, but the anterior process is sinuous and curves ventrally.

facts.statement: Paranthodon's premaxilla lacks teeth, a trait shared with most stegosaurs.
facts.quote: The premaxilla also lacks any teeth, like in every stegosaur except Huayangosaurus where the premaxilla is preserved.

facts.statement: Unlike most other stegosaurs, the prezygapophysis of Paranthodon faces dorsally.
facts.quote: Unlike in all other stegosaurs except Stegosaurus, the prezygapophysis faces dorsally.

facts.statement: Paranthodon is currently classified as a stegosaur related to Stegosaurus, Tuojiangosaurus, and Loricatosaurus.
facts.quote: Currently, Paranthodon is classified as a stegosaur related to Stegosaurus, Tuojiangosaurus, and Loricatosaurus.

facts.statement: Initially, the fossils now known as Paranthodon were classified as ankylosaurians by Broom.
facts.quote: Initially, when Broom assigned the name Palaeoscincus africanus to the Paranthodon fossils, he classified them as an ankylosaurian.

facts.statement: A 1981 review by Galton and Coombs confirmed that Paranthodon is a stegosaurid from the Lower Cretaceous.
facts.quote: A subsequent review by Galton and Coombs in 1981 instead confirmed Nopcsa's interpretation, redescribing Paranthodon as a stegosaurid from the Lower Cretaceous.

facts.statement: A 2017 analysis by Susannah Maidment and Thomas Raven resolved Paranthodon's relationships within Stegosauria.
facts.quote: An elaboration upon this analysis was published in 2017 by Susannah Maidment and Thomas Raven, and it resolved relationships within Stegosauria much more.

facts.statement: Paranthodon was the first species uncovered in the Kirkwood Formation in South Africa.
facts.quote: The Kirkwood Formation is in South Africa, and many fossils of different species and genera have been discovered in it, with Paranthodon being the first uncovered.

facts.statement: The Kirkwood Formation, where Paranthodon was found, dates from the Late Jurassic to Early Cretaceous, between 145.5 and 130 million years ago.
facts.quote: The formation is of a Late Jurassic to Early Cretaceous age, with the oldest deposits from the Tithonian, about 145.5 million years ago, and the youngest rocks being from the Valanginian, about 130 million years ago.

facts.statement: If teeth from Ethiopia are correctly attributed to Paranthodon, its geographic range extends significantly.
facts.quote: If the referral of teeth from Ethiopia to Paranthodon is correct, then the taxon's geographic range is extended significantly.

facts.statement: Teeth found at the 151-million-year-old Mugher locality in southern and eastern Africa may extend Paranthodon's known age and range.
facts.quote: The Mugher locality is approximately 151 million years old, about 14 million older than has previously been suggested for Paranthodon, as well as across both southern and eastern Africa.

facts.statement: The genus Paranthodon was named by Nopcsa in 1929.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Nopcsa, 1929

facts.statement: The species Paranthodon africanus was originally described by Broom in 1912.
facts.quote: species_authority: (Broom, 1912)

facts.statement: It is debated whether the type material of Paranthodon actually bears synapomorphies of Stegosauria, despite phylogenetic analyses placing it within the group.
facts.quote: Even though phylogenetic analyses recognise Paranthodon as a stegosaurid, the type material bears no synapomorphies of Stegosauria.

facts.statement: Paranthodon africanus was a thyreophoran stegosaurian dinosaur that lived approximately 145 to 140 million years ago during the Berriasian and Valanginian stages of the Early Cretaceous in what is now Africa.
facts.quote: Paranthodon africanus es la única especie conocida del género extinto Paranthodon (del griego παρά- [para-] 'junto a' y Anthodon) de dinosaurio tireóforo estegosáurido, que vivió a principios del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 145 y 140millones de años, entre el Berriasiense y el Valanginiense, en lo que hoy es África.

facts.statement: Paranthodon was an armored dinosaur with plates measuring about 4 meters long, 1.8 meters high, and weighing 1000 kg.
facts.quote: Paranthodon fue un dinosaurio acorazado con placas, que medía alrededor 4m de largo, 1.8 de alto y un peso de 1000kg.

facts.statement: Thomas R. Holtz Jr. estimated that Paranthodon measured 5.0 meters in length and weighed between 454 and 907 kg.
facts.quote: Thomas R. Holtz Jr. estimó que el animal medía 5.0 metros de largo y pesaba entre 454 y 907 kg.

facts.statement: Paranthodon had an elongated snout that was convex on the top, though not extremely so.
facts.quote: El hocico es alargado, aunque no extremadamente, y convexo en la parte superior.

facts.statement: The teeth of Paranthodon featured a prominent primary crest.
facts.quote: Los dientes tienen una cresta primaria prominente.

facts.statement: Thirteen teeth are preserved in Paranthodon, but the sockets extend to the back of the maxilla, suggesting there may have been more in life.
facts.quote: En Paranthodon se conservan trece dientes, pero los alvéolos se extienden a medida que se recorre hasta la parte posterior del maxilar, por lo que posiblemente hubiera más en vida.

facts.statement: The teeth of Paranthodon have a central crest with five less prominent crests on each side.
facts.quote: Los dientes tienen una cresta media, con cinco crestas menos prominentes a cada lado.

facts.statement: Like all stegosaurs, the denticles on the teeth of Paranthodon are rounded at the tips, contrasting with ankylosaurs.
facts.quote: Como todos los estegosaurios, los dentículos de los dientes son redondeados en las puntas, en contraste con los anquilosáuridos.

facts.statement: Unlike Kentrosaurus and Stegosaurus, Paranthodon possesses a prominent buccal margin, a crest alongside the row of teeth, similar to Huayangosaurus.
facts.quote: También como Huayangosaurus, pero a diferencia de Kentrosaurus y Stegosaurus, Paranthodon posee una marginación bucal prominente, una cresta al lado de la fila de dientes.

facts.statement: Wear is absent on most teeth of Paranthodon, similar to Huayangosaurus, suggesting it likely lacked tooth occlusion.
facts.quote: Los dientes de Paranthodon conservan el desgaste, pero el desgaste está ausente en la mayoría de los dientes, similar a Huayangosaurus, lo que significa que es probable que Paranthodon careciera de oclusión entre los dientes.

facts.statement: Only two fragments of a vertebra are known for Paranthodon, revealing few anatomical details.
facts.quote: Como solo se conocen dos fragmentos de una vértebra, se pueden observar pocos detalles anatómicos.

facts.statement: In 1845, amateur geologists William Guybon Atherstone and Andrew Geddes Bain discovered several fossils near Dassieklip in the Cape Province, in the Bushman River valley.
facts.quote: En 1845, los geólogos aficionados William Guybon Atherstone y Andrew Geddes Bain descubrieron varios fósiles cerca de Dassieklip, provincia del Cabo, en el valle del río Bushman.

facts.statement: This discovery was the first dinosaur find in Africa and the Southern Hemisphere.
facts.quote: Este fue el primer hallazgo de dinosaurio en África y en el hemisferio sur.

facts.statement: In 1849 and 1853, Bain sent some of the fossils to paleontologist Richard Owen for identification.
facts.quote: En 1849 y 1853, Bain envió algunos de los fósiles al paleontólogo Richard Owen para su identificación.

facts.statement: In 1876, Owen named a series of specimens Anthodon serrarius, basing the genus name on the resemblance of the teeth to a flower.
facts.quote: En 1876 Owen nombró una serie de especímenes de la colección Anthodon serrarius, basando el nombre del género en la semejanza de los dientes con una flor.

facts.statement: The holotype, consisting of a partial skull (BMNH 47337), left jaw (BMNH 47338), and neck (BMNH 47338) with bone fragments and impressions of the anterior skull and vertebrae (BMNH 47337a), was assigned to Anthodon.
facts.quote: El holotipo, un cráneo parcial, BMNH 47337, la mandíbula izquierda BMNH 47338, el cuello BMNH 47338 que incluye fragmentos óseos e impresiones de la parte anterior del cráneo y las vértebras BMNH 47337a se asignaron a Anthodon.

facts.statement: In 1909, Robert Broom visited the collection of the British Museum of Natural History.
facts.quote: En 1909, Robert Broom visitó la colección del Museo Británico de Historia Natural.

facts.statement: Broom kept the name Anthodon for the pareiasaur but identified the other fossil as a member of the genus Palaeoscincus, naming the new species Paleoscincus africanus in 1912.
facts.quote: Broom mantuvo el nombre Anthodon para el pareiasaurio, pero identificó el otro fósil como un miembro del género Palaeoscincus, nombrando la nueva especie Paleoscincus africanus en 1912.

facts.statement: In 1929, Franz Nopcsa provided a new name, Paranthodon owenii, unaware of Broom's prior publication, because DMS Watson believed the jaw should be distinguished from Anthodon.
facts.quote: En 1929, Franz Nopcsa, sin tener conocimiento de la publicación anterior de Broom, proporcionó un segundo nombre de novela, ya que DMS Watson creía que la mandíbula debería diferenciarse de Anthodon.

facts.statement: Following modern conventions, the species name was later modified to owenii.
facts.quote: Siguiendo las convenciones modernas, el nombre de la especie fue posteriormente modificado a owenii.

facts.statement: Walter P. Coombs incorporated both names into current nomenclature in his 1971 dissertation as the new combination Paranthodon africanus, because Paranthodon was the first new generic name for the fossils and africanus was the first new specific name.
facts.quote: Ambos nombres fueron incorporados a la nomenclatura actual por Walter P. Coombs en su disertación de 1971 como la nueva combinación Paranthodon africanus ya que el nombre Paranthodon fue el primer nombre genérico nuevo para los fósiles y africanus fue el primer nombre específico nuevo.

facts.statement: Paranthodon is considered to belong to the family Stegosauridae, being a close relative of Kentrosaurus, within the subfamily Stegosaurinae.
facts.quote: Se considera que Paranthodon pertenece a la familia Stegosauridae, siendo pariente cercano de Kentrosaurus, dentro de la subfamilia Stegosaurinae.

facts.statement: Paranthodon was found in the upper part of the Kirkwood Formation in the Cape Province, South Africa.
facts.quote: Paranthodon fue encontrado en la parte superior de la Formación Kirkwood, en la provincia del Cabo en Sudáfrica.

facts.statement: Broom concluded that Owen had mixed the skull, teeth, and partially distorted jaw of a pareiasaur with the partial upper jaw of a dinosaur, BMNH 47338, which were from two different species.
facts.quote: Concluyó que Owen había mezclado el cráneo, los dientes y la mandíbula parcialmente distorsionados de un pareiasaurio y la mandíbula superior parcial de un dinosaurio, BMNH 47338, que eran de dos especies diferentes.

facts.statement: The holotype of Paranthodon was found in the Kirkwood Formation, dated to the Berriasian to early Valanginian ages.
facts.quote: El holotipo de Paranthodon , BMNH 47338, se encontró en una capa de la Formación Kirkwood que se ha fechado entre las edades Berriasiana y Valanginiana temprana.

facts.statement: The holotype consists of the back of the snout containing the toothed maxilla, the posterior caudodorsal ramus of the premaxilla, parts of the nasals, and some isolated lower jaw teeth.
facts.quote: Consiste en la parte posterior del hocico, que contiene el maxilar con dientes, la rama caudodorsal posterior del premaxilar, parte de las nasales y algunos dientes aislados probablemente de la mandíbula inferior.

facts.statement: An additional specimen, BMNH (now NHMUK) R4992, was assigned to Paranthodon based on isolated teeth sharing the same morphology as the holotype.
facts.quote: Se le asignó un espécimen adicional basada en una dentición, BMNH (ahora NHMUK) R4992, que incluía solo dientes aislados que compartían la misma morfología que los del holotipo.

facts.statement: Lee Hall and Mark Goodwin referred two partial teeth discovered in the Mugher Mudstone of Ethiopia to Paranthodon in 2011.
facts.quote: Dos de los dientes parciales descubiertos fueron referidos a Paranthodon por Lee Hall y Mark Goodwin en 2011.

facts.statement: The teeth lack any autapomorphies of Paranthodon and were referred to an indeterminate stegosaurid in 2008.
facts.quote: Los dientes no tienen ninguna autapomorfia de Paranthodon, y fueron referidos a un estegosáurido indeterminado en 2008.

facts.statement: In 2018, the teeth were identified as lacking distinctive stegosaurian features and were designated as an indeterminate Thyreophora.
facts.quote: Los dientes fueron identificados en 2018 como carentes de características distintivas de los estegosaurios, por lo que fueron designados como un Thyreophora indeterminado.

facts.statement: Paranthodon is currently classified as a stegosaurid related to Stegosaurus, Tuojiangosaurus, and Loricatosaurus.
facts.quote: Actualmente, Paranthodon está clasificado como un estegosáurido relacionado con Stegosaurus, Tuojiangosaurus y Loricatosaurus.

facts.statement: Initially, when Broom assigned the name Palaeoscincus africanus to the Paranthodon fossils, he classified them as ankylosaurians.
facts.quote: Inicialmente, cuando Broom asignó el nombre Palaeoscincus africanus a los fósiles de Paranthodon, los clasificó como anquilosaurianos.

facts.statement: In 1978, Coombs did not follow Nopcsa's classification, keeping Paranthodon as an ankylosaurian like Broom, though only as Ankylosauria incertae sedis.
facts.quote: Coombs en 1978 no siguió la clasificación de Nopcsa, manteniendo a Paranthodon como anquilosauriano, como Broom, aunque sólo lo clasificó como Ankylosauria incertae sedis.

facts.statement: A later review by Galton and Coombs in 1981 confirmed Nopcsa's interpretation, redescribing Paranthodon as a Late Cretaceous stegosaurid.
facts.quote: Una revisión posterior de Galton y Coombs en 1981 confirmó en cambio la interpretación de Nopcsa, redescribiendo Paranthodon como un estegosáurido del Cretácico Superior.

facts.statement: Paranthodon was distinguished from other stegosaurids by a long and wide posterior process of the premaxilla, teeth in the maxilla with a very large cingulum, and large crests on the tooth crowns.
facts.quote: Paranthodon se distinguía de otros estegosáuridos por un proceso posterior largo y ancho de la premaxila, dientes en el maxilar con un cíngulo muy grande y grandes crestas en las coronas de los dientes.

facts.statement: Not all these features were considered valid in a 2008 review of Stegosauria, and the only autapomorphy found was the possession of a partial secondary bony palate in the maxilla.
facts.quote: No todas estas características se consideraron válidas en una revisión de 2008 de Stegosauria y la única autapomorfia encontrada fue la posesión de un segundo paladar óseo parcial en el maxilar.

facts.statement: A 2010 analysis including almost all stegosaurian species found Paranthodon outside Stegosauridae in a polytomy with Tuojiangosaurus, Huayangosaurus, Chungkingosaurus, Jiangjunosaurus, and Gigantspinosaurus.
facts.quote: Un análisis de 2010 que incluyó casi todas las especies de estegosaurianos encontró que Paranthodon estaba fuera de Stegosauridae y en una politomía con Tuojiangosaurus , Huayangosaurus, Chungkingosaurus, Jiangjunosaurus y Gigantspinosaurus.

facts.statement: Susannah Maidment and Thomas Raven published an elaboration of this analysis in 2017, resolving many relationships within Stegosauria.
facts.quote: Susannah Maidment y Thomas Raven publicaron una elaboración de este análisis en 2017, y resolvió mucho más las relaciones dentro de Stegosauria.

facts.statement: Paranthodon was grouped with Tuojiangosaurus, Huayangosaurus, and Chunkingosaurus as the most basal true stegosaurians.
facts.quote: Paranthodon se agrupó con Tuojiangosaurus, Huayangosaurus y Chunkingosaurus como los estegosaurianos verdaderos más basales.

facts.statement: Other analyses have found Paranthodon to be closely related to Tuojiangosaurus, Loricatosaurus, and Kentrosaurus within Stegosaurinae.
facts.quote: Otros análisis han encontrado que Paranthodon está estrechamente relacionado con Tuojiangosaurus, Loricatosaurus y Kentrosaurus dentro de Stegosaurinae.

facts.statement: Although phylogenetic analyses recognize Paranthodon as a stegosaurid, the type material does not present synapomorphies of Stegosauria.
facts.quote: Aunque los análisis filogenéticos reconocen a Paranthodon como un estegosáurido, el material tipo no presenta sinapomorfias de Stegosauria.

facts.statement: The parent group of Paranthodon is Stegosauridae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Stegosauridae

facts.statement: The type species of Paranthodon is Paranthodon africanus.
facts.quote: Type species: Paranthodon africanus

facts.quote: Time range: Berriasian to Valanginian (143.1 to 132.6 million years ago)
